issues.existing: long translucent ribbons trailing from the poles
issues.observed: the long translucent trailing material reads as the figures' own gowns, veils and sashes; nothing is confirmable as a ribbon attached to a pole
issues.evidence: The streaming pale sheets originate at the figures' shoulders, waists and hems and fall away behind their bodies. The poles themselves read as bare shafts with small twigs and leaves. The only thing hanging from a pole that I could resolve is a single small pendant near the top of the central figure's raised shaft. Some pale wisps near the upper left pole are indistinguishable from mist and the overhanging branches.

issues.existing: the central figure stands nearest the viewer, the others arranged in a loose ring around her
issues.observed: the five are spread across the frame width in a shallow left-to-right arc at broadly similar depth, not a ring around the central figure
issues.evidence: All five heads sit on a shallow arc across the frame; the second and fourth are set slightly further back and higher in the haze, while the first and fifth are at the sides at roughly the central figure's depth. No figure is placed behind or on the far side of the central figure, which a ring arrangement would require. 'Nearest the viewer' for the central figure is defensible — she is the lowest and most fully rendered — but 'a loose ring around her' is not supported, and the haze makes depth cues weak enough that I could not establish the arrangement precisely either.

issues.existing: the central figure stands nearest the viewer, the others arranged in a loose ring around her
issues.observed: The other four are not arranged in a ring around the central figure. My blind notes record the five as a loose cluster across the middle band of the frame — two on the viewer-left, one pushed forward at centre, two on the viewer-right — i.e. a shallow arc that opens toward the viewer, with the central figure standing in front of it rather than enclosed by it. No figure stands in front of her or directly behind her.
issues.evidence: My blind observation states verbatim: 'the five figures form a loose cluster across the middle band of the frame, not a straight line: two on the left, one pushed forward at centre, two on the right', and separately 'the centre figure stands nearest the viewer and lowest; the second and fourth figures are set furthest back and sit highest in the frame'. The depth ordering therefore runs front-to-back from the centre figure to the flanking pair, which is a flanking arc, not a surrounding ring.
